newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: INSTANT VIEW - Portuguese March inflation.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Portuguese March inflation.

text.p: The following are analysts' reactions to the 0.1 percent month-on-month rise in the Portuguese consumer price index (CPI)in March, for a 2.5 percent year on year rise, announced by the National Statistics Institute (INE) on Tuesday.

"It is the confirmation of the absence of inflationary pressures in the economy. It increases the room for the Bank of Portugal to cut interest rates, supported by an escudo strong and firm against the mark."

"The year-on-year rate (2.5 percent) surprised me. I only expected it in April or May. We are on the road to fulfilling the prices criteria (for the single currency) set down in the Maastricht Treaty. I suppose that at this moment, we are some 0.3 percentage points from meeting the criteria. We will have to wait until the end of the week to see if there will be a cut in interest rates (by the Bank of Portugal). To have a cut we will have to see the mark-escudo exchange rate sustained below or close to 100.50. Nevertheless, I hope that the Bank will cut its three rates if the rate is not above 100.80 to the mark."
JOAO VERMELHO, ANALISTA DA CENTRAL DE INVESTIMENTOS

"The inflation number for March is pretty good and below our expectations. This number can help sustain the bourse in its upward trend but the performance of foreign bourses has been the decisive factor (recently)."

"It is a very favourable number. I think that, in terms of inflation, the Bank of Portugal now must have room to cut rates. I would like to see the trend in the non-tradable goods, but with these numbers, it must have been pretty good in March and below that of February (when non-tradeable sector prices rose 4.8 percent year-on-year). This improves the inflation outlook for the end of the year and if prices behave as expected during the coming months, we could end up below 2.5 percent."
